Project namespaces ​

Context ​

ADR#9316364013 fixes the directories at the repository root, and ADR#5842232571 splits source by language toolchain. Both read as if the repository holds one thing. A repository that hosts several, such as products, platform systems and experiments, spreads each of them across every root directory, with no single place that holds all of one thing.

Most of the time that is fine: each thing shows up as a namespace segment the tools already provide, such as a crate prefix, a protobuf package path or a chart name. It stops being fine when one thing has its own owner and release cadence, or is an experiment that has to be deleted without touching anything else. A survey of our repositories found those cases solved ad hoc, with experiments/ at the root and product names as root directories next to the language workspaces.

Putting maturity in the path, as experiments/ does, makes graduation a move. A move breaks import paths, CI filters, ownership rules and links, so an experiment that succeeds changes its address exactly when people start depending on it.

Resolution ​

The root project ​

  • You MUST treat the repository root as a project with no name. Everything not moved into projects/ lives in the root directories, and is not limited to code that named projects share.
  • You SHOULD tell apart the things the root holds by a namespace segment inside the root directories: a crate or package name prefix, a protobuf package path, an image or chart name, an OpenTelemetry registry domain.

Named projects ​

  • You SHOULD NOT create projects/ until a thing needs isolation that a namespace segment cannot give it: its own owner, its own release cadence, or deletion as a unit. You MUST NOT create it in anticipation of a second thing, and a repository that holds one thing never has it.
  • You MAY then move that thing into projects/<project>/, named in kebab-case. You MUST use the same name as the prefix of the crates, packages, images and charts it produces.
  • You MUST place what a project owns inside projects/<project>/: its language workspaces per ADR#5842232571, its docs/ and its README.md. A project that runs its own mise tasks MUST be a nested mise configuration root per ADR#6647967335.
  • You MUST NOT nest projects/ inside a project.
  • You MUST NOT encode maturity or kind in the path. experiments/, labs/, sandbox/, products/ and apps/ are not containers for projects. You MUST state the lifecycle in a line directly under the title of the project's README.md, as Status: experimental, Status: active or Status: deprecated, and change that line instead of moving the directory.
  • You SHOULD move a project to its own repository when nothing requires it to share this one. Extraction takes projects/<project>/ as the new root, plus every path under its namespace segment in the shared root directories. Every root path the dependency graph lists for the project MUST first be published as a versioned package the project consumes, or be copied into it, so the extracted repository builds on its own.

Shared root directories ​

  • You MUST keep .github/ at the repository root, because GitHub reads it nowhere else.

  • You SHOULD keep .config/, devops/, otel/ and the schema source directories proto/, wit/, openapi/ and asyncapi/ at the repository root, shared by the root project and every named project. One buf module, one semantic convention registry and one operational estate that see every project at once catch conflicts that separate copies hide.

  • You MUST lay out those root directories to hold several projects side by side, each under its namespace segment: proto/<org>/<project>/, wit/<project>/, openapi/<project>/, asyncapi/<project>/, otel/registry/<vendor>/<project>/, devops/docker/images/<project>-*/, devops/helm/charts/<project>-*/.

  • You MAY nest any of those directories inside projects/<project>/ when the project cannot share the root copy, such as a separate buf module or an operational estate no other project touches. The nested copy follows the same ADR as the root one, and the project's share MUST NOT then also live in the root copy.

    txt
    .
├── .github/  .config/  devops/  otel/  proto/   # shared, one segment each
├── rsworkspace/  docs/                           # the root project
└── projects
    └── <project>
        ├── README.md                             # Status: experimental
        ├── .config/mise/tasks/                   # its own tasks only
        ├── .config/mise/lib/
        ├── rsworkspace/
        ├── goworkspace/
        └── docs/

Dependencies ​

  • You MUST keep dependencies pointing inward from the root. A project MAY depend on the root workspaces and the shared root directories. The root MUST NOT depend on a project, and a project MUST NOT depend on another project. Code two projects need lives in the root.
  • You MUST derive the dependency graph from the toolchain manifests, such as cargo metadata, go list -deps and the pnpm workspace, plus the namespace segments in the shared root directories. You MUST NOT maintain a list of dependencies by hand.
  • You MUST expose the graph as a mise task that prints, as JSON, every project with the paths it owns and the root paths it depends on. The root project owns every path outside projects/.
  • You MUST compute CI path filters, sparse checkouts and affected-project selection from that output, and MUST NOT write the paths into a workflow by hand. A change under .config/ affects every project.

Consequences ​

  • Each project carries its own lockfile per language, so its dependency versions drift from the root and from other projects. That is the price of isolation, and the reason the namespace segment stays the default.
  • A project that depends on code in the root takes it as a path dependency across workspaces instead of as a workspace member, and the graph picks the edge up from the manifest.
  • A project's sparse checkout is its directory, the shared root directories and the root paths the graph lists. The shared directories are taken whole, which keeps git in cone mode.
  • Graduating an experiment is a one-line change to its README.md, and deleting one is deleting its directory and its namespace paths.
